transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Ava Chen (Oberon - Lead ML Eng), Samir Rao (Oberon - DevOps), Lina Gomez (Oberon - CISO)

Summary:
Maya: quick run through the SDKs, show python snippet, show typescript snippet, auth, env vars, quickstarts, and next steps to kick off PoC.

00:00 Maya: all right everyone thanks for joining, afternoon, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, joining me is Jordan our solutions engineer.
00:10 Ava: hey thanks Maya, excited to see the SDKs, we looked at the docs, a few questions on auth and network.
00:25 Jordan: great, we'll start with a quick overview then jump into the Python quickstart; code will be in the repo link, https://redwood.ai/sdk/quickstart (note: link in notes).
00:40 Jordan: Python snippet, basically pip install redwood; set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var, then from redwood import Client; client = Client(); client.generate(...)
00:58 Samir: sorry can you repeat the env var pattern, we run everything via k8s secrets and want to map in CI/CD.
01:10 Jordan: yeah so we recommend using KMS for key rotation, store in your secret manager and mount as env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, for Dedicated/Private we can do mTLS or SSO via SAML for team access.
01:30 Lina: we require SSO and audit logs; does Redwood support SAML/SCIM and can we have audit logs forwarded?
01:42 Maya: yes - we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and can ship audit logs to your syslog or S3; we'll share the SOC2 pack; for on-prem we also support customer-managed KMS.
02:05 Jordan: quick Typescript example: npm install @redwood/inference; import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.chat.create({ messages:[{role:'user',content:'hi'}] });
02:30 Ava: nice, what about streaming responses? we need low-latency streaming for chat.
02:40 Jordan: streaming is supported in both SDKs, WebSocket or server-sent events; in Node TS you'll use client.chat.stream and in Python an iterator over stream chunks. There are small differences in behaviour across runtimes; we'll include the examples.
03:10 Samir: regarding network access for Private deployment, we need to understand VPC peering vs on-prem connectors; any docs?
03:25 Maya: yes, for Private we do VPC peering or you can deploy the private runtime on your infra; Jordan will follow up with the network diag requirements and a checklist.
03:45 Jordan: also to note, if you pick Dedicated hosted capacity we can restrict egress and provide dedicated subnets and egress IPs, reduces compliance burden.
04:05 Ava: on the topic of cost, how do we estimate token costs and how does batching affect latency?
04:20 Jordan: good Q; Redwood Optimize suggests batching levels; for low-latency chat we keep batch size small and use KV caching to reduce tokens; we'll run a benchmark baseline for your workload as an action item.
04:50 Ava: perfect, for the PoC we want a baseline: 1k concurrent small chat sessions, 4k tokens/session peak, target p95 latency < 600ms.
05:10 Jordan: noted; I'll propose a test plan. we'll run tests against both hosted API and a dedicated config so you can compare unit costs and p95.
05:40 Maya: I'll send our quickstarts repo and sample code; Jordan will prepare the benchmark plan and sample dataset.
06:00 Samir: minor question on SDK versions, for TS we use node 18+, any breaking changes?
06:15 Jordan: we follow semver; SDKs have minor changes, we pin in the quickstart, but we recommend integrating via package.json lockfile in CI.
06:40 Ava: can you show the Python quickstart file layout? like config, env, sample app.
06:55 Jordan: sure — structure in the repo: /python-quickstart/README.md, main.py, requirements.txt; main shows auth via env var, init client, call generate/chat, handle streaming and errors.
07:20 Jordan: example main.py pseudo:
    import os
    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
    resp = client.chat.create(messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Summarize Q3'}])
    print(resp.text)
08:00 Ava: ok that looks straightforward, what about local dev vs deployed env — do we run the same calls?
08:10 Jordan: yes, same API surface; for on-prem you set REDWOOD_API_URL to your private endpoint and use client = Client(base_url=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_URL')) plus certs if mTLS.
08:30 Samir: does Redwood provide terraform modules for infra setup for VPC peering and subnets?
08:42 Maya: we have sample terraform snippets and deployment docs; Jordan will attach the network checklist and terraform examples.
09:05 Lina: security question: how long are logs stored and can we set retention per customer?
09:20 Maya: yes retention is configurable, hosted default 90 days but enterprise customers can extend or ship logs to their S3 and use their retention policies.
09:35 Ava: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest?
09:44 Jordan: yes, we integrate with KMS/HSM with Bring-Your-Own-Key for Private and Dedicated; again details in the security pack we'll share.
10:10 Ava: about model versions: can we pin models and do canary rollouts?
10:20 Jordan: yes—model pinning, versioning, canary rollouts, A/B tests in the Console; you can set fallback policies and automatic regressions alerts tied to prompt sets.
10:45 Samir: for the PoC we need 99.9% uptime during test hours; what SLA can we expect for Dedicated?
10:55 Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA doc in the pack.
11:15 Ava: how do we authenticate service-to-service in k8s? token rotation strategies?
11:25 Jordan: recommend short-lived tokens with CI rotation and KMS-backed secrets; for SSO use SAML for user auth and mTLS or mutual OIDC for services depending on network.
12:00 (short silence / crosstalk)
12:15 Maya: demo time — I'll share my screen to show the quickstart repo and run the Python sample (note: transcription might miss exact command outputs)
12:32 Jordan: running python main.py... hitting the hosted endpoint, response in 180ms, streaming chunked, showing how to handle incremental flush.
13:05 Ava: that latency looks good; did you run with quantization enabled?
13:14 Jordan: we used a quantized LLM variant for that test; quantization reduces memory and cost but can slightly change outputs; we can recommend quant profiles per workload via Redwood Optimize.
13:40 Samir: do you support on-the-fly quantization or we need model variants prepared?
13:55 Jordan: model variants are prepared during onboarding; runtime picks kernels and quant paths based on profiles automatically.
14:20 Ava: next steps and responsibilities?
14:30 Maya: recap — Maya send quickstart links and security docs; Jordan prepare benchmark plan and terraform samples; Ava confirm compliance contacts and upload network diagram; schedule PoC kickoff.
14:50 Ava: timeline — aiming to start PoC next week, procurement sign-off by end of month.
15:05 Maya: perfect, we'll follow up via email with the repo and docs and propose times for the PoC kickoff.
